content.what_it_is: MATLAB Case A composite-beach comparison script described at L1-L27. It imports measured/reference variables from A.mat and seven station files (L28-L36), scales station times by 1/10 and adds 261.7 (L39-L47), performs a no-op second station loop (L49-L57), converts 600 samples of seven gauge series to centimeters (L59-L67), vertically separates paired gauge 4..9 series (L69-L85), and overlays measured and numerical series for gauges 4..10 (L88-L133).
unresolved: Both length-based loops at L39-L57 use length(n4) while indexing n5 through n10; unequal station lengths can either index past shorter inputs or leave tails of longer inputs untransformed.
Assignments L50-L56 write each second-column element back to itself, so the entire second loop has no effect.
The L59-L67 conversion loop requires at least 600 elements in every g4..g10 series imported at L29 without checking lengths.

Every measured plot uses the same imported t with g4..g10 (L89,L94,L99,L104,L109,L114,L119) without checking vector lengths, and station inputs are indexed as two-column matrices without shape validation.
Only gauges 4..9 are vertically offset at L69-L85; gauge 10 is not, but the script gives no statement clarifying whether this asymmetry is intentional.

The legend at L133 supplies only two labels after fourteen plot objects were added at L89-L121; MATLAB associates them with only the first two plotted objects, which are g4 measured and n4 numerical rather than all seven pairs explicitly.
